items.title: 9.5.1 Calculating H3O+ ions from Ka and the molar concentration of a weak acid

blocks.title: Sample Problem 9.3
blocks.problem: Calculate the concentration of [H₃O⁺] in a 0.1 M (mol dm⁻³) solution of acetic acid [CH₃COOH], given that the acid dissociation constant Ka is 1.8 × 10⁻⁵.
blocks.answer: The concentration [H₃O⁺] in the solution is approximately 1.34 × 10⁻³ mol dm⁻³.

blocks.title: Quick Check 9.3
blocks.text:
a) The pH of a 0.10 M solution of formic acid, HCOOH, at 25°C is 2.38. Calculate Ka for formic acid at this temperature.
b) Calculate the concentration of [H₃O⁺] in a 0.1 M solution of nitrous acid [HNO₂], given that the acid dissociation constant Ka is 4 × 10⁻⁴.
c) A vinegar sample is found to have 0.837 M CH₃COOH. Its hydronium ion concentration is found to be 3.86 x 10⁻³ mol dm⁻³. Calculate Ka for acetic acid.
